initial_source_grounded_issues.reason: The SPARQL constraint only reports a violation when a case displacement is greater than DUI. It therefore permits DUI values greater than the greatest waterline-case displacement, even though the source requires DUI to be the displacement corresponding to the greatest displacement. The query does not establish equality with the maximum case value.
initial_source_grounded_issues.expected: For every admitted ship, DUI must equal the greatest valid displacement among all waterline cases used to determine the UIWL. Both DUI below the maximum and DUI above the maximum must be rejected.
initial_source_grounded_issues.suggestion: Replace the one-sided FILTER EXISTS test with logic that rejects any case value greater than DUI and also rejects DUI when no case has a value equal to the maximum valid case displacement, or otherwise directly express equality to the maximum case value.

functional_changes: Replaced one-sided greater-case test with greater-case OR no-equal-case test
Expanded embedded-query prefixed IRIs to full IRIs
Preserved target, quantity datatype/unit and cardinality constraints outside query changes

Review the complete supplied SHACL against source, schema and declared research scope. Return one JSON object matching expected_response_schema. Review every query/branch and all represented source obligations. No fixtures, labels, counterpart records, expected verdicts or known solution are supplied. Never request them. Shape messages and execution success are not proofs of correct logic.

The packet supplies full_candidate once. Use candidate_location rather than quoting code: {candidate_version, candidate_sha256, unit: "lines" or "characters", start, end}. Lines are one-based inclusive; character offsets are zero-based half-open Unicode positions. The server extracts exact code. Reference previous_location against previous_candidate when assessing changes. For missing code, locate a real insertion anchor. Never invent ranges or stale hashes.

Evidence uses concise request-local E IDs. The server binds each to immutable content and provenance hashes. Use only IDs in this packet. source_evidence_id must identify a SOURCE entry; source_excerpt, when asserted, must be an exact nonempty substring preserving source whitespace. evidence_id/evidence_excerpt must match supplied text; RDF_FACT permits only one equivalent explicit ground triple with identical RDF terms, lexical forms, datatype and language. No inference, numeric coercion, blank-node equivalence or ontology-wide lookup. A valid reference does not prove the interpretation. Caller admission is an experimental assumption with provenance, not a legal-source quotation or independently certified eligibility.

Decisions: ACCEPT (no issues, all changes supported and prior issues resolved); REJECT (actionable source/schema-backed code issue); UNRESOLVED (material missing information); REQUEST_EVIDENCE (up to three bounded catalog source/schema requests). Unsupported claims, uncertainty and absent evidence must remain explicit. For every material retrieval gap include unchecked {scope: gap_id, material, reason}. Material unchecked scope prevents ACCEPT. Activation/deactivation and full query correctness are separate obligations; resolving scope proves neither arithmetic nor compliance.

For each functional change_id return ONE change_assessments entry, with source support, current/previous locations and reason. If removal_required is true, removal_disposition must be SUPPORTED_REMOVAL, REPLACED, REGRESSION or UNRESOLVED and the reason must assess lost numeric/unit/query/target obligations and any replacement. There is no separate removal response list or pre-issued repair permission. Source-supported removal of an excessive old restriction is allowed; checker silence alone is not support. REGRESSION/UNRESOLVED requires a corresponding issue/change_id; UNRESOLVED requires an unresolved-context issue and decision.

Reconcile exactly the original prior_issues IDs; code edits alone do not resolve an issue. Empty prior_issues requires empty reconciliations. Format feedback does not create accepted issues or authorize repair; the original candidate/prior state and request binding remain unchanged. Echo candidate_version, candidate_sha256 and review_request_id. Correct all listed format errors in a complete response.

Use proposed_path_role PROPERTY for a path ending at the named property, NUMERIC_OPERAND for traversal through that quantity property to the declared numeric predicate. Do not concatenate unrelated owner branches or relabel units as conversion. Vocabulary/domain/range facts do not alone establish ownership or legal eligibility.

execution_probe is an actual candidate-bound engine observation, with full logs preserved in server artifacts. A static translation/binding warning is not a confirmed engine failure. Successful execution does not establish complete branch coverage or regulatory adequacy. Nested/library shapes need no target if reachable from an active root. Material unsupported activation, deactivation or unknown bindings prevent acceptance. Never invent selectors, target fixture identities, infer eligibility from missing data or weaken source obligations to silence diagnostics.


Response correction and operand pairing: An issue about several operands may use operands[], each with a unique operand_id and its own property, proposed_path and explicit proposed_path_role (PROPERTY or NUMERIC_OPERAND); optional proposed_unit/proposed_datatype belong to that operand. The same declared representation evidence applies. Legacy scalar proposals are still checked and are not discarded when operands are present. Never pair one property's name with another property's path.

A proven internal pairing inconsistency may return exact validation_errors using the existing shared response-correction allowance. Correct or withdraw the inconsistent proposal; do not rewrite the candidate. Keep original candidate, evidence and prior issues unchanged. Rejected response issues are not prior state. An unknown path or genuine source/schema contradiction remains blocking: report representation_disposition UNRESOLVED_CONTRADICTION (and uncertainty), never disguise a contradiction as formatting. Evidence citations do not prove an interpretation. No requirement-specific calculation answer is supplied.

<BEGIN_SHACL>
@prefix nltl: <https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#> .
@prefix sh: <http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#> .
@prefix rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#> .
@prefix rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#> .
@prefix xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#> .
@prefix dcterms: <http://purl.org/dc/terms/> .
@prefix qudt: <http://qudt.org/schema/qudt/> .
@prefix unit: <http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/> .

nltl:I2_004_UpperIceWaterlineDisplacementShape
    a sh:NodeShape ;
    sh:targetClass nltl:ship ;
    sh:property [
        a sh:PropertyShape ;
        sh:path nltl:upperIceWaterlineDisplacement ;
        sh:minCount 1 ;
        sh:maxCount 1 ;
        sh:node nltl:I2_004_QuantityValueShape ;
        sh:severity sh:Violation ;
        sh:message "Each admitted ship must have exactly one upper ice waterline displacement DUI, represented as a quantity in metric kilotonnes." ;
    ] ;
    sh:property [
        a sh:PropertyShape ;
        sh:path nltl:hasUpperIceWaterlineCase ;
        sh:minCount 1 ;
        sh:node nltl:I2_004_UpperIceWaterlineCaseShape ;
        sh:severity sh:Violation ;
        sh:message "Each admitted ship must have at least one upper ice waterline case." ;
    ] ;
    sh:sparql [
        a sh:SPARQLConstraint ;
        sh:select """
            SELECT $this
            WHERE {
                FILTER NOT EXISTS {
                    $this <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#type> ?admittedType .
                    ?admittedType <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#subClassOf>* <https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#ship> .
                }
            }
        """ ;
        sh:message "The focus node is not typed as nltl:ship under the RDFS class hierarchy required by the caller-admitted population." ;
        sh:severity sh:Violation ;
    ] ;
    sh:sparql [
        a sh:SPARQLConstraint ;
        sh:select """
            SELECT $this
            WHERE {
                $this <https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#upperIceWaterlineDisplacement> ?upperQuantity .
                ?upperQuantity <http://qudt.org/schema/qudt/numericValue> ?upperValue ;
                                <http://qudt.org/schema/qudt/unit> <http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/KiloTON_Metric> .

                FILTER (
                    EXISTS {
                        $this <https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#hasUpperIceWaterlineCase> ?greaterCase .
                        ?greaterCase <https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#waterlineCaseDisplacement> ?greaterQuantity .
                        ?greaterQuantity <http://qudt.org/schema/qudt/numericValue> ?greaterValue ;
                                        <http://qudt.org/schema/qudt/unit> <http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/KiloTON_Metric> .
                        FILTER (?greaterValue > ?upperValue)
                    }
                    ||
                    NOT EXISTS {
                        $this <https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#hasUpperIceWaterlineCase> ?equalCase .
                        ?equalCase <https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#waterlineCaseDisplacement> ?equalQuantity .
                        ?equalQuantity <http://qudt.org/schema/qudt/numericValue> ?equalValue ;
                                       <http://qudt.org/schema/qudt/unit> <http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/KiloTON_Metric> .
                        FILTER (?equalValue = ?upperValue)
                    }
                )
            }
        """ ;
        sh:message "The ship displacement DUI must equal the greatest displacement among the waterline cases used to determine the UIWL." ;
        sh:severity sh:Violation ;
    ] ;
    rdfs:label "I2-004 upper ice waterline displacement shape"@en ;
    rdfs:comment "Represents IACS UR I2 clause I2.1.2.2: the ship displacement DUI is the displacement, in kt, corresponding to the upper ice waterline (UIWL). Where multiple waterlines are used for determining the UIWL, the displacement is to be determined from the waterline corresponding to the greatest displacement."@en ;
    rdfs:comment "The target is limited to the caller-admitted synthetic design population of nltl:ship records. External Polar Class eligibility, construction-date eligibility, and legally governing edition applicability are not independently inferred or enforced by this shape."@en ;
    rdfs:comment "The source applicability statement is retained: This UR applies to Polar Class ships according to UR I1. The referenced UR I1 context and edition are caller-supplied contextual evidence, not independently verified eligibility predicates."@en ;
    dcterms:source [
        rdfs:comment "file=data/requirements/IACS_I2_full.txt; document_sha256=7ad8d57459782b70809da479380584a57cf259c66d9ff286811c0248b02732d2; selection_start=0; selection_end=1304; selection_sha256=c6e77eb821ae603a13c191d7eb5073821d353775215f91d431bb454faf9207cb; section_ids=PREAMBLE,I2.1,I2.1.1,I2.1.2,I2.1.2.1,I2.1.2.2."@en
    ] ;
    dcterms:source [
        rdfs:comment "Source selection manifest sha256=36c8b4e14715ec0e62f77b4d278a08ee5776a42ff869d433d66a8afb2beef41d; included_characters=2448; original_characters=62501; omitted_sections=108. Missing necessary evidence remains unresolved."@en
    ] ;
    rdfs:comment "Unresolved source references retained for review: UR I1 (source offset 320-325); UR I1 section I1.1.6 (source offset 50772-50778); UR I2 section I2.13 (source offset 50843-50848). These references do not activate or deactivate this shape."@en .

nltl:I2_004_UpperIceWaterlineCaseShape
    a sh:NodeShape ;
    sh:class nltl:upperIceWaterlineCase ;
    sh:property [
        a sh:PropertyShape ;
        sh:path nltl:waterlineCaseDisplacement ;
        sh:minCount 1 ;
        sh:maxCount 1 ;
        sh:node nltl:I2_004_QuantityValueShape ;
        sh:severity sh:Violation ;
        sh:message "Each upper ice waterline case must have exactly one waterline-case displacement in metric kilotonnes." ;
    ] ;
    rdfs:label "I2-004 upper ice waterline case shape"@en ;
    rdfs:comment "The case represents a waterline used for determining the UIWL. Multiple cases are permitted; the greatest valid case displacement determines DUI."@en .

nltl:I2_004_QuantityValueShape
    a sh:NodeShape ;
    sh:class qudt:QuantityValue ;
    sh:property [
        a sh:PropertyShape ;
        sh:path qudt:numericValue ;
        sh:minCount 1 ;
        sh:maxCount 1 ;
        sh:datatype xsd:decimal ;
        sh:severity sh:Violation ;
        sh:message "A displacement quantity must have exactly one decimal numeric value." ;
    ] ;
    sh:property [
        a sh:PropertyShape ;
        sh:path qudt:unit ;
        sh:minCount 1 ;
        sh:maxCount 1 ;
        sh:hasValue unit:KiloTON_Metric ;
        sh:severity sh:Violation ;
        sh:message "A displacement quantity must use exactly the metric kilotonne unit http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/KiloTON_Metric." ;
    ] ;
    rdfs:label "I2-004 displacement quantity value shape"@en ;
    rdfs:comment "Quantity serialization uses qudt:numericValue with xsd:decimal and qudt:unit with an IRI, as declared by the locked JSON-LD representation context."@en .
<END_SHACL>

Decisions: ACCEPT (no issues, all changes supported and prior issues resolved); REJECT (actionable source/schema-backed code issue); UNRESOLVED (material missing information); REQUEST_EVIDENCE (up to three bounded catalog source/schema requests). Unsupported claims, uncertainty and absent evidence must remain explicit. For every material retrieval gap include unchecked {scope: gap_id, material, reason}. Material unchecked scope prevents ACCEPT. Activation/deactivation and full query correctness are separate obligations; resolving scope proves neither arithmetic nor compliance.

For each functional change_id return ONE change_assessments entry, with source support, current/previous locations and reason. If removal_required is true, removal_disposition must be SUPPORTED_REMOVAL, REPLACED, REGRESSION or UNRESOLVED and the reason must assess lost numeric/unit/query/target obligations and any replacement. There is no separate removal response list or pre-issued repair permission. Source-supported removal of an excessive old restriction is allowed; checker silence alone is not support. REGRESSION/UNRESOLVED requires a corresponding issue/change_id; UNRESOLVED requires an unresolved-context issue and decision.

Reconcile exactly the original prior_issues IDs; code edits alone do not resolve an issue. Empty prior_issues requires empty reconciliations. Format feedback does not create accepted issues or authorize repair; the original candidate/prior state and request binding remain unchanged. Echo candidate_version, candidate_sha256 and review_request_id. Correct all listed format errors in a complete response.

Use proposed_path_role PROPERTY for a path ending at the named property, NUMERIC_OPERAND for traversal through that quantity property to the declared numeric predicate. Do not concatenate unrelated owner branches or relabel units as conversion. Vocabulary/domain/range facts do not alone establish ownership or legal eligibility.

execution_probe is an actual candidate-bound engine observation, with full logs preserved in server artifacts. A static translation/binding warning is not a confirmed engine failure. Successful execution does not establish complete branch coverage or regulatory adequacy. Nested/library shapes need no target if reachable from an active root. Material unsupported activation, deactivation or unknown bindings prevent acceptance. Never invent selectors, target fixture identities, infer eligibility from missing data or weaken source obligations to silence diagnostics.


Response correction and operand pairing: An issue about several operands may use operands[], each with a unique operand_id and its own property, proposed_path and explicit proposed_path_role (PROPERTY or NUMERIC_OPERAND); optional proposed_unit/proposed_datatype belong to that operand. The same declared representation evidence applies. Legacy scalar proposals are still checked and are not discarded when operands are present. Never pair one property's name with another property's path.

A proven internal pairing inconsistency may return exact validation_errors using the existing shared response-correction allowance. Correct or withdraw the inconsistent proposal; do not rewrite the candidate. Keep original candidate, evidence and prior issues unchanged. Rejected response issues are not prior state. An unknown path or genuine source/schema contradiction remains blocking: report representation_disposition UNRESOLVED_CONTRADICTION (and uncertainty), never disguise a contradiction as formatting. Evidence citations do not prove an interpretation. No requirement-specific calculation answer is supplied.
